_comment._chop: OPEN QUESTION, NOT RESOLVED BY THIS CONFIG. The source is modulated at 4.70 Hz and fit_com HOLDS its last coordinate through a dark stretch (AYLP_FRAME_REJECTED) rather than reporting a gap; prbs_test does not inspect that flag and will correlate the held samples as if they were data. Measured stretches run to 201 frames against max_lag 48 and a 255-frame burst, so a dark stretch can span an entire correlation window. Zero-order-hold segments bias the correlogram toward LONGER apparent lag. Either run this on a CW source, or check the fit_com rejection rate in the log and treat the result as suspect if it is not near zero.

params._roi_note: ROI and exposure copied from steering_par_fsp.json so this measures the plant the loop actually runs against. Exposure is part of the delay being measured: change it and this number changes. ROI re-derived 2026-08-06 to 1084/418 (find_roi put the beam at 1088/406; the residual is the 4-px/2-px ASI ROI grid) -- the earlier 644/318 was an unverified ASI662MM carry-over. The beam walks several px per hour: re-probe with contrib/probe_frame.json and re-derive once |park| exceeds ~2 px.

pipeline._note: fit_com, matching steering_par_fsp.json exactly. The centroid computation is inside the delay being measured, so it HAS to be the one the loop uses -- when steering moved from center_of_mass to fit_com (2026-08-06) this file had to move with it or it would be timing a sensor the loop no longer contains. fit_com is also the quieter estimator (hf 0.271 px vs 0.639 for thresholded center_of_mass), which tightens the correlation peak.
pipeline._cost: fit_com costs p50 17.4 us / p99 27.0 us per frame against a 433 us frame period. That cost is CONSTANT across the burst and so contributes a fixed offset to the measured delay, exactly as it does in the loop -- which is the point. It does not smear the peak.
pipeline._provenance: Values MEASURED 2026-08-06 by contrib/com_survey_run.sh at this ROI/exposure: beam sigma 6.55 px, amplitude 213.9 over background 1.74. window 55 = +/-4 sigma; sigma_min/max and min_amplitude are 0.3x/4x/0.1x of measured. RE-RUN com_survey_run.sh and re-derive after any refocus or source change.

params._reacquire: 300, matching steering_par_fsp.json and NOT the old 10. The 4.70 Hz source modulation produces ~6 dark stretches per second, median 3 frames but p90 49 and max 201 (measured 2026-08-06). At 10 the window would drop acquisition several times per second and re-search mid-burst, which is a sensor discontinuity landing directly in the correlogram. At 300 those stretches take the hold path instead. SEE _chop IN THE HEADER: holding is not free for a correlation either.

pipeline._note1: THE TEST. Drives element 1 (x) and watches element 1 of the CoM ([y, x]); y stays at 0 command, i.e. parked at 0 V.
pipeline._note2: quiet_frames 128 is both the rest between bursts (so each one starts from the same state) and the room the correlator needs: it must be at least max_lag, or one burst's tail overlaps the next burst's start.
pipeline._note3: neg_lags 24 buys the noise floor. Nothing can respond before the command, so the scatter over those acausal lags is what the onset threshold and the peak/noise ratio are judged against. It is not just sensor noise -- the linear autocorrelation of a finite 127-chip m-sequence has sidelobes of a few percent.
pipeline._phase_band: 20-200 Hz. The top matches the freq_end of conf_bode_par_x.json's sweep, so this tau and that one are fit over the same band and are directly comparable. Raising phase_f_hi past the plant's own roll-off starts fitting noise, not delay.

params.config: x/tilt loop delay through the PARPORT DAC (DAC81404, spi link, mmio, +-5 V range, mirror parked at 0 V), no coarse stage, ch0=y parked / ch1=x driven at scale -1.0 V/unit. ASI290MM 64x64 ROI 1084/418, exp 400, gain 0, fs ~2310 Hz, fit_com 55x55 sigma_init 6.55. Compare the phase-slope tau IN FRAMES against a bode sweep TAKEN ON THIS SAME CAMERA/ROI/EXPOSURE -- conf_bode_par_x.json now writes fsm_bodex_par3 -- and against the fsp delay/delay_frac in steering_par_fsp.json. Do NOT compare against fsm_bodex_par2.dat's 2.763 fr: that was 32x32/exp50 at fs 3788 Hz on the pre-swap camera, and neither its frame count nor its 0.729 ms survives the change.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC, wired exactly as steering_par_fsp.json: ch0 = y/tip, ch1 = x/tilt, scale [1, -1], offset 0. skip_unchanged stays off -- a PRBS changes the code every frame anyway, and a skipped write would be a missing edge in the very stimulus being correlated.
pipeline._range: +-5 fixed, no auto-ranging: a range change mid-burst would put a one-frame glitch into the response and land in the correlogram as a spurious lag.
